title: Quasi-finite etale shriek preserves constructible cohomology
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. All derived categories below are the bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For a separated finite-type morphism $h:T\to B$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and a compactification $c=(j:T\hookrightarrow\overline T,p:\overline T\to B)$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper, set $Rh_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Assume $h:T\to B$ is also quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] and of finite presentation. If $K\in D^+(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ has constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], then $Rh_!^cK$ has constructible cohomology on $B_{\Et}$ for every compactification $c$. In particular this applies to a closed immersion of finite presentation.

source.place: Tags 0GK3, label lemma-qf-f-shriek-constructible, and 0GKM, label lemma-Rf-shriek-for-quasi-finite; finite-ring bounded-below specialization

proof.text: Apply the finitely presented Zariski main factorization to $h$: its separatedness, quasi-finiteness, finite presentation and qcqs target are precisely the hypotheses. Obtain $T\xrightarrow{a}T_1\xrightarrow{g}B$ with $a$ a quasi-compact open immersion, $g$ finite and finitely presented, $T_1$ qcqs, and $h=g\circ a$. A finite morphism is proper: apply the finite-morphism permanence statement (c) to $g$ and the proper identity of $B$. Hence $d=(a,g)$ is a compactification permitted in the statement.

For a constructible module sheaf $F$ on $T$, extension by zero along $a$ is constructible on $T_1$, as follows directly from its strata. Inside $a(T)$ its restriction is $F$, by the extension-by-zero unit isomorphism; the unit is $\Lambda$-linear and its inverse is linear because its underlying abelian map is bijective. On the complementary closed subscheme all geometric stalks of the restriction are zero, by the extension-by-zero stalk formula and the inverse-image stalk formula. The map from this restriction to the zero sheaf is bijective on all geometric stalks, hence an isomorphism on underlying sets, and therefore on modules. Take the images of the finitely many strata for $F$ and add the complementary closed subscheme, with value the zero module. They are disjoint locally closed strata and cover $T_1$. Their subsets are constructible: $a(T)$ is retrocompact since $a$ is quasi-compact; if $V$ is retrocompact open in $T$, then for every quasi-compact open $W$ of $T_1$, $V\cap a^{-1}(W)$ is quasi-compact because $a^{-1}(W)$ is quasi-compact, so $a(V)$ is retrocompact open in $T_1$. Images of the Boolean generators $V\setminus V^{\prime}$ are thus the same differences of retrocompact opens in $T_1$; the complement of $a(T)$ is constructible too. Restrictions to the old strata are the given finite locally constant modules, and to the new stratum are the constant zero module. This meets every clause of the constructible-sheaf definition.

source.place: Tag 0GK3 (lemma-qf-f-shriek-constructible), separated case, open extension step; expanded using Etale Cohomology 0F70 (lemma-jshriek-open) and the constructible strata definition

proof.text: Finite direct image $g_*$ is exact by the finite-direct-image exactness statement. The module version follows from the abelian version: kernels and cokernels of module-sheaf maps carry the induced $\Lambda$-action on their abelian kernels and cokernels; thus an abelian-exact image sequence is module-exact. Consequently the right derived functor on module sheaves is the degreewise functor $g_*$: applying $g_*$ to a quasi-isomorphism remains a quasi-isomorphism, since exactness carries its acyclic cone to an acyclic cone, so applying it to an injective resolution gives the same derived object as applying it to the original complex. Extension by zero is exact on module sheaves as well. For an exact functor $E$, kernels, images and quotients are preserved, so $H^q(E(C))=E(\ker d^q/\operatorname{im}d^{q-1})=E(H^q(C))$. For a bounded-below representative of $K$ this gives $Rh_!^dK=Rg_*a_!K\cong g_*a_!K$ and $H^q(Rh_!^dK)\cong g_*a_!H^q(K)$ for every integer $q$. Both exact functors preserve the lower bound; no upper bound or finite Tor amplitude is used.

source.place: Tag 0GKM (lemma-Rf-shriek-for-quasi-finite), finite higher direct image vanishing; 0GK3 first sentence, exactness and cohomology

proof.text: Each $H^q(K)$ is constructible by hypothesis. Step 2 makes $a_!H^q(K)$ constructible; apply finite finitely presented pushforward constructibility to $g:T_1\to B$ to make $g_*a_!H^q(K)$ constructible. Step 3 identifies these sheaves with the cohomology of $Rh_!^dK$. For any compactification $c$, compactification independence supplies $Rh_!^cK\cong Rh_!^dK$. Applying cohomology transfers the same finite stratification and local trivializations along this isomorphism. Thus all cohomology sheaves of $Rh_!^cK$ are constructible for every $c$.

For the final assertion retain the qcqs scheme assumptions. A closed immersion of finite presentation is finite by the closed-immersion finiteness lemma. Its fibre over a point is empty or the spectrum of a residue field, so every fibre point is isolated. It is of finite type and separated (its diagonal is an isomorphism). Thus it is quasi-finite under the cited definition, and all the hypotheses just used hold.
